blocks.x: Zero-trust across a merged group estate, audit findings closed ahead of the supervisory review and phishing-resilient access for 11,000 staff

Identity withheld, an insurance group formed from three mergers, inheriting three identities, three VPNs and one supervisory review on the calendar. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline assessment counted the merger debt: 4,200 accounts with standing privileged access, and the last penetration test had found the same two findings three times because remediation was tracked in a spreadsheet nobody owned.
The supervisory finding list was public within the group; the deadline was not negotiable, and the estate could not be frozen to fix it.

We ran the zero-trust program as gates, not a project: identity consolidated behind phishing-resilient MFA with privileged access JIT, network segmentation by data class rather than by merger lineage, and the supervisory findings tracked as evidence-backed closure items the regulator could walk. Legacy access died on a schedule the business signed, not in a big-bang cutover.

Figures on this page are the client's, reproduced with permission. Method notes and measurement designs are available under NDA.
Start with the diagnostic, not the contract: the same diagnostic that baselined this program takes two weeks, and a scoped proposal follows only if the delta justifies it.
